# Sirach 45 — Disagreement Log

**Chapter:** Sirach 45 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 19

---

## Disagreement 1 — 45:1, "From him" vs. "From Jacob"

**EMET:** "From him he brought forth a man"
**LOGOS:** "From Jacob he brought forth a man"
**PNEUMA:** "From Jacob came a man"
**Issue:** The antecedent is Jacob (44:23). EMET leaves the pronoun; LOGOS/PNEUMA supply the name for clarity. Supplying the name is more readable.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA supplies "Jacob" following LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 45:2, "awesome fear of his enemies" vs. "his enemies stood in awe"

**EMET:** "made him great in the awesome fear of his enemies"
**LOGOS:** "his enemies stood in awe of him"
**PNEUMA:** "his enemies trembled before him"
**Issue:** Greek en phobō echthrōn = in the fear of enemies. EMET preserves the genitive structure; LOGOS/PNEUMA invert to active construction. EMET's structure is more literal.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "so that his enemies stood in awesome fear of him" — combining both readings.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 45:3, "By his words he caused signs to cease" vs. "By his word he made signs cease"

**EMET:** "By his words he caused signs to cease"
**LOGOS:** "By his word he made signs cease"
**PNEUMA:** "By his word Moses stopped the plagues"
**Issue:** Greek en logois = by his words. "Signs" vs. "plagues" — Greek sēmeia = signs/miracles. PNEUMA's "plagues" interprets narrowly. EMET/LOGOS retain "signs."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "By his word he made signs cease" — "word" (singular) is more elevated.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 45:4, "meekness" vs. "gentleness"

**EMET:** "faithfulness and meekness"
**LOGOS:** "faithfulness and meekness"
**PNEUMA:** "faithfulness and gentleness"
**Issue:** Greek praotēta = meekness, gentleness. EMET/LOGOS agree on "meekness" (more traditional for Moses: Num. 12:3); PNEUMA prefers "gentleness."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "meekness" — the connection to Num. 12:3 ("the man Moses was very meek") is deliberate.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 45:5, "thick cloud" vs. "dark cloud"

**EMET:** "led him into the thick cloud"
**LOGOS:** "led him into the dark cloud"
**PNEUMA:** "led him into the dark cloud"
**Issue:** Greek gnophos = thick darkness, gloom (not simply cloud). LOGOS/PNEUMA "dark cloud" is better; EMET "thick cloud" is an older rendering.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "dark cloud" — gnophos specifically denotes the divine darkness of theophany.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 45:5, "enlighten Israel" vs. "teach Jacob"

**EMET:** "to teach Jacob the covenant and Israel his judgments"
**LOGOS:** "to teach Jacob the covenant and enlighten Israel with his decrees"
**PNEUMA:** "to teach Jacob the covenant and enlighten Israel with God's decrees"
**Issue:** Greek photisai = to enlighten. EMET "his judgments" doesn't capture the light metaphor; LOGOS/PNEUMA "enlighten" is better.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "teach Jacob the covenant and enlighten Israel with his decrees."

---

## Disagreement 7 — 45:7, "girded him with a glorious belt" vs. "girded him about with a glorious robe"

**EMET:** "girded him with a glorious belt"
**LOGOS:** "girded him about with a glorious robe"
**PNEUMA:** "dressed him in a glorious robe"
**Issue:** Greek periezdsen = girded around. "Belt" (EMET) refers to the priestly sash; "robe" (LOGOS) is broader. The Greek zōnē = belt, girdle. EMET is more literal.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "girded him with a glorious robe" — in context this is the full garment described in subsequent verses.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 45:8, "perfect glory" vs. "full glory"

**EMET:** "clothed him with perfect glory"
**LOGOS:** "clothed him in perfect glory"
**PNEUMA:** "clothed him in the fullness of splendor"
**Issue:** Greek teleiotēta doxēs = the fullness/completeness of glory. "Perfect glory" (EMET/LOGOS) is literal; "fullness of splendor" (PNEUMA) expands to two nouns.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "perfect glory" (EMET/LOGOS).

---

## Disagreement 9 — 45:8, "emblems of strength" vs. "symbols of authority"

**EMET:** "the emblems of strength"
**LOGOS:** "the symbols of authority"
**PNEUMA:** "the insignia of power"
**Issue:** Greek en krataiomasin = in strengths/mighty things. "Emblems of strength" (EMET) is literal; "symbols of authority" (LOGOS) interprets the function; "insignia of power" (PNEUMA) is similar.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "symbols of authority" as more natural English.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 45:9, "very many golden bells" vs. "many gold bells"

**EMET:** "very many golden bells all around"
**LOGOS:** "many gold bells all around"
**PNEUMA:** "many golden bells all around"
**Issue:** Greek polla rhoia = many bells/pomegranate-bells. "Very many" vs. "many" — Greek does not indicate superlative here. LOGOS/PNEUMA more accurate.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "many golden bells all around."

---

## Disagreement 11 — 45:10, "oracle of judgment" vs. "oracle of decision"

**EMET:** "the oracle of judgment, the Urim and Thummim"
**LOGOS:** "the oracle of decision, the Urim and Thummim"
**PNEUMA:** "the oracle of judgment, the Urim and Thummim"
**Issue:** Greek logion kriseos = oracle of judgment. "Judgment" (EMET/PNEUMA) is most literal; "decision" (LOGOS) softens to the oracular function.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "oracle of judgment" — the legal/oracular weight of krisis should be preserved.

---

## Disagreement 12 — 45:10, "twisted crimson" vs. "twisted scarlet"

**EMET:** "twisted crimson, the work of a craftsman"
**LOGOS:** "twisted scarlet, the work of an artisan"
**PNEUMA:** "twisted scarlet — a craftsman's work"
**Issue:** Greek kokkinou klōstou = twisted scarlet/crimson thread. "Scarlet" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is more standard for kokkinos; "crimson" (EMET) is slightly different.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "twisted scarlet" (LOGOS).

---

## Disagreement 13 — 45:12, "seal of holiness" vs. "sacred inscription"

**EMET:** "engraved with the seal of holiness"
**LOGOS:** "engraved with the sacred inscription"
**PNEUMA:** "engraved with the sacred inscription"
**Issue:** Greek sphragidi agiasmatou = seal/signet of sanctification. The reference is to Ex. 28:36 — "Holy to the LORD" engraved on the gold plate. "Seal of holiness" (EMET) is more literal; "sacred inscription" (LOGOS) is more descriptive.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "engraved with the seal of holiness" — preserving the sphragis/seal imagery.

---

## Disagreement 14 — 45:15, "filled his hands" vs. "ordained him"

**EMET:** "Moses filled his hands"
**LOGOS:** "Moses ordained him"
**PNEUMA:** "Moses ordained him"
**Issue:** Greek eplēsen tas cheiras = he filled his hands. "Filling the hands" is the technical term for ordaining a priest (Ex. 28:41 — LXX uses the same phrase). LOGOS/PNEUMA interpret it as "ordained." EMET preserves the idiom.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "Moses ordained him" — while the literal idiom is interesting, the functional meaning is more accessible. A footnote would note the idiom.

---

## Disagreement 15 — 45:18, "Strangers banded against him" vs. "Outsiders plotted against him"

**EMET:** "Strangers banded against him and envied him"
**LOGOS:** "Outsiders plotted against him and envied him"
**PNEUMA:** "outsiders ganged up on him, jealous of him"
**Issue:** Greek allotrioi = foreigners, outsiders. In context these are Israelites who were "outsiders" to the priestly calling. "Outsiders" (LOGOS) is more precise than "Strangers."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "Outsiders" (LOGOS).

---

## Disagreement 16 — 45:20, "made the glory of Aaron great" vs. "multiplied the glory"

**EMET:** "he made the glory of Aaron great and gave him his inheritance"
**LOGOS:** "he multiplied the glory of Aaron and gave him his inheritance"
**PNEUMA:** "He increased Aaron's glory and gave him his inheritance"
**Issue:** Greek emegalunen = he magnified/made great/multiplied. "Magnified" would be the most literal; "multiplied" (LOGOS) and "increased" (PNEUMA) are similar.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "He magnified the glory of Aaron."

---

## Disagreement 17 — 45:21, "bread for them in abundance" vs. "their bread in abundance"

**EMET:** "He prepared bread for them in abundance"
**LOGOS:** "He prepared their bread in abundance"
**PNEUMA:** "He prepared food for them in plenty"
**Issue:** Greek artous = breads/loaves. "Bread" vs. "food" — the Greek specifically mentions bread (showbread context).
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "bread" over "food."

---

## Disagreement 18 — 45:23, "zealous in the fear of the Lord" vs. "ablaze with zeal for the Lord"

**EMET:** "zealous in the fear of the Lord"
**LOGOS:** "zealous in the fear of the Lord"
**PNEUMA:** "ablaze with zeal for the Lord"
**Issue:** Greek zēlōsas en tō theō = being zealous for God. EMET/LOGOS agree; PNEUMA adds "ablaze" which is vivid but not in the Greek.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS: "zealous in the fear of the Lord."

---

## Disagreement 19 — 45:26, "good things may not be abolished" vs. "prosperity may not vanish"

**EMET:** "their good things may not be abolished"
**LOGOS:** "their prosperity may not vanish"
**PNEUMA:** "their prosperity never fades"
**Issue:** Greek ta agatha = good things, prosperity. "Good things" (EMET) is literal; "prosperity" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) interprets. In context the material well-being of the priesthood is meant.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "prosperity may not perish" — more vivid than "vanish."

---

*Total disagreements logged: 19*
